speaker: Patient
text: 42-year-old Caucasian male. The patient reports experiencing visible blood in his urine accompanied by discomfort in his right flank. He denies any recent trauma to the area. He mentions a series of urinary tract infections over the past few years but has not been on renal dialysis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Kidney Stone (Nephrolithiasis)

Given your history of recurrent UTIs and the classic presentation of right flank pain with hematuria, a kidney stone is the most likely cause. Are you currently experiencing nausea or vomiting, and have you noticed any changes in your urine stream, such as thinning or interruption? REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis with microscopy and urine culture. REQUEST IMAGES: Right Kidney Ultrasound.
